reason: I'll fit the digestive tract into its named lower-body slot, starting one of the two assembly goals.
expectation: The abdominal portion of the digestive tract will be placed in the lower body, with space left for the urinary organs.

alternatives.reason: Joining the studied arm to the chest also advances a goal, but I'll start with the lower body.

effect: The gut is in place, with its upper food pipe continuing toward the chest; the urinary organs still need fitting.
reaction: It is helpful to see how the gut fits without cutting off its route upward.
reason: I'll fill the remaining named slot to finish assembling the lower body's organs.
expectation: The kidneys, ureters and bladder will fit into the lower body alongside the digestive tract.

effect: The lower-body organs are fitted, with the urinary and digestive outlets separate. Next I'll work on the chest.
reaction: Seeing where the kidneys and bladder fit makes the assembly clearer.
reason: I'll attach the arm we built earlier to start the chest assembly goal.
expectation: The studied arm should join the chest at the shoulder, keeping its muscles and bones together.

alternatives.reason: The lymph network also needs to join the chest, but I'll attach the arm first.

effect: The studied arm is attached, including its blood vessels and nerves; the other arm and lymph network still need joining.
reaction: The shoulder connections make it feel like part of the body rather than a separate model.
reason: I'll attach the other arm to complete the pair.
expectation: The supplied arm will join the opposite shoulder while the first arm stays in place.

alternatives.reason: The lymph network also needs connecting, but I'll finish the arms first.

effect: Both arms are attached; the lymph network remains to be joined to the chest.
reaction: The second arm went where expected.
reason: I'll connect the lymph network to advance the remaining chest goal; it's the only offered combination.
expectation: The lymph vessels will join the chest model, with their return route connecting to a vein.

effect: The lymph network is aligned with the chest's existing vein, completing the chest goal and opening the goal to join the body regions.
reaction: It's useful to see that the return route connects without adding a duplicate junction.
reason: I'll join the chest and lower body to meet the new goal; it's the only offered combination.
expectation: The two regions will connect at the diaphragm, keeping their fitted organs and routes in place.

effect: The chest and lower body are joined, and the open back channel shows where the spine belongs.
reaction: The separate routes through the diaphragm make the joined regions easier to picture.
reason: I'll fit the head and spine into the trunk to meet the new goal; it's the only offered combination.
expectation: The spine should fit into the back channel, connecting the head and nerves to the trunk.

effect: The head and spine are connected to the trunk, and the remaining goal is to fit the skin covering.
reaction: Seeing the nerves and blood routes serve the same muscles ties earlier chapters together.
reason: I'll fit the skin covering to meet the new goal; it's the only offered combination.
expectation: The covering should fit over the body with the repaired segment at its original forearm location.

effect: The skin covering completed the body while keeping the earlier organs and repaired scar visible in the cutaway. All chapter goals are complete.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the separate parts together without losing the earlier details.

mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the chest and lower body was most worthwhile: it showed how the diaphragm separates them while important routes still pass between them.

leastWorthwhile.text: Attaching the second arm was predictable after attaching the first, so it added less to my understanding.

surprise.text: I hadn't pictured the lymph return connecting to the same neck vein already in the chest model.

arbitrary.text: None felt purposeless, but the final fittings mostly followed named goals and the only offered combinations rather than requiring me to figure out compatibility.

continue.text: I would try another chapter if it explored a new connection between body systems. The final assembly tied things together, though the repeated fittings were less interesting.
